::: {.callout-important}
## The sequence is fixed; calendar dates come later

The milestones below are anchored to the course content students need before
each stage. They do not set calendar dates or change the working quiz and
midterm placements. Exact Blackboard opening and closing times will be
announced after the assessment calendar is finalized.
:::

## Why The Projects Use Stages

Each project is worth 10% of the course grade and is completed by a group.
Staging prevents students from receiving every file and requirement at once,
gives beginners a concrete next action, and keeps Project 2 validation genuinely
unseen until the model plan is recorded.

A week label identifies the intended course stage, not an additional weekly
assignment. Project work is separate from the routine 90-120 minute practice
target in the [weekly workload guide](../weeks/workload-guide.qmd).

## Project 1: MATLAB Numerical Investigation

| Course stage | Milestone | Students receive | Student action or evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Week 3** | Preview | Public project page, data dictionary, report template, required filenames, and a view of the building-energy question | Confirm the group and group number; inspect the task and file structure. No project analysis is due. |
| **Week 4** | Assigned package release | One group-specific MATLAB ZIP through Blackboard | Extract the ZIP without renaming its contents; check the group identifier; open the data and starter files; run the starter far enough to reach its first marked task. |
| **Week 5** | Guided readiness checkpoint | Instructor-selected support using the released package | Show that the main script finds the assigned data, the supplied RMSE function passes its hand-checkable test, and at least one checked fit or figure can be reproduced. This is a progress checkpoint, not a second project submission. |
| **After Week 5** | Completion window | Blackboard group submission area and final checklist | Complete the analysis, PDF, source, and generated results CSV; rerun from a clean folder; submit one group package. The exact deadline is set later in coordination with Quiz 2. |

No new Project 1 technical requirement is introduced after Week 5. The
completion window is for finishing, checking, reconciling the PDF with the
generated results, and submitting—not for adding another analysis method.

### Project 1 Blackboard Gates

1. The preview is public and contains no group-specific data.
2. The assigned ZIP is visible only to the corresponding Blackboard group.
3. The readiness checkpoint checks setup and progress; no extra report is
   created for it.
4. The final Blackboard Group Assignment contains one upload per group with the
   exact files listed on the [Project 1 page](project-1-eda.qmd).

## Project 2: R Modeling And Validation

| Course stage | Milestone | Students receive | Student action or evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Weeks 9-10** | Preview | Public project page, data dictionary, report template, required filenames, and explanation of the training/validation split | Confirm the group; inspect the task and file structure. No model is selected and no project analysis is due. |
| **Week 12** | Training package release | One group-specific R training ZIP through Blackboard; no validation outcomes | Extract the ZIP; verify the group identifier; run the starter to its first marked task; begin code-based cleaning, row checks, summaries, and exploratory figures. Do not invent the final model before Week 13 instruction. |
| **After Week 13** | Frozen-model-plan gate | A short Blackboard group checkpoint containing the required plan fields | Record the response, predictors, formula, primary coefficient, baseline, validation metric, and one expected failure condition. The plan is frozen before any validation file is opened. |
| **Week 14** | Validation release and application | One group-specific validation ZIP, released in a common window after the frozen-plan gate | Apply the frozen training model; save one prediction per validation row; calculate MAE and RMSE; run the declared sensitivity check. Explain any later deviation rather than silently replacing the frozen plan. |
| **Week 15** | Rehearsal and completion window | Final checklist and Blackboard group submission area | Run the complete workflow from a clean folder; reconcile the PDF, R source, results CSV, and prediction CSV; complete the AI-use appendix and contribution statement; submit one group package. The exact deadline is announced later. |

The validation ZIP is not released early to an individual group. At the common
release gate, only groups with a recorded model plan should receive it; a missed
checkpoint requires instructor follow-up rather than an informal early or late
release.

### The Frozen Plan Is Short

The checkpoint records only the choices needed to protect the validation stage:

1. numeric response;
2. selected predictors;
3. exact R formula;
4. coefficient chosen for interpretation;
5. mean-response baseline;
6. validation metric;
7. one condition under which the planned conclusion may fail.

This checkpoint does not require a polished report or finished model
diagnostics. Those are completed after the relevant Week 13-14 teaching.

## Blackboard Release Map

| Blackboard item | Visibility | Opens when | Closes or locks when |
|---|---|---|---|
| Project 1 preview | All students | Week 3 preview | Remains available |
| Project 1 assigned ZIP | Corresponding group only | Week 4 release gate | Remains available through submission |
| Project 1 group assignment | Corresponding group | Completion window opens | Exact deadline announced later |
| Project 2 preview | All students | Weeks 9-10 preview | Remains available |
| Project 2 training ZIP | Corresponding group only | Week 12 release gate | Remains available through submission |
| Frozen-model-plan checkpoint | Corresponding group | After Week 13 model instruction | Locks before validation release |
| Project 2 validation ZIP | Corresponding group only | Common Week 14 release gate after the plan checkpoint | Remains available through submission |
| Project 2 group assignment | Corresponding group | Week 15 completion window | Exact deadline announced later |

For each final group submission, one student uploads the package and every group
member checks the Blackboard receipt and retains a local copy. Group membership,
release visibility, filenames, and downloaded ZIP contents are checked in the
live Blackboard course before student release.

## What Remains Deferred

- exact calendar dates and times;
- the exact length and delivery of the quizzes and midterm;
- the final Project 1 deadline within its post-Week-5 completion window;
- the exact Blackboard closing times for the Project 2 plan and final package.

The order of the gates is established even while those dates remain open.
